components.css: .ds-toast { width: 340px; overflow: hidden; background: #FFFFFF; color: #0F172A; border: 1px solid #CBD5E1; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 12px 28px -6px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.24); animation: ds-toast-in 0.32s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-toast-band { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 36px; padding: 0 4px 0 12px; background: #166534; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: "Overpass", system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 0.82rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; animation: ds-band-wipe 0.42s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 0.05s both; } .ds-toast-close { margin-left: auto; width: 36px; height: 36px; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: inherit; cursor: pointer; } .ds-toast-close:hover { background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12); } .ds-toast-close:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #F59E0B; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-toast-text { display: block; padding: 10px 14px 12px; font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.98rem; line-height: 1.4; } @keyframes ds-toast-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } } @keyframes ds-band-wipe { from { clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0); } to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-toast, .ds-toast-band { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The state of every product and every action reads like a construction-site sign (after NTC 1461): a header band carrying one uppercase word, legible at a distance and in full sun. The world is built for the contractor holding a phone on site, with gloves on and the sun on the screen, so information that decides a purchase (availability, REF, price, unit) sits at fixed positions on every card and never has to be hunted for.

The surface is a pale working floor (`background`) with slate structure: a slate bar on top, a near-black slate footer, white panels framed by a 1px rule. Colour is spent on meaning, not decoration. Three sign colours say DISPONIBLE, POCAS UNIDADES and AGOTADO; amber, in addition, marks the one path the visitor is on (add to cart, cart, quote). Hierarchy comes from scale: prices set at sign size in Overpass, reading text in Atkinson Hyperlegible. Density is honest: a 2-column grid on phones, 4 to 5 columns on desktop, and a list view for people who already know what they want.

The world explicitly rejects the white store of soft rounded cards with a promotional banner, and the earlier "slate wall with lettering" of v1.3.

Scope of what is built: the public store (top bar, home, catalog, product detail, toasts, footer) is redesigned in this world. Cart, checkout, auth, account, legal pages and the admin panel inherit the tokens only and have not been redesigned yet; new work on them should adopt the components below rather than their current inline styles.
keyCharacteristics: One shared signature, the sign band, used by product cards, the detail sign, toasts, alerts and empty states.
Amber only on the active path; everything else is slate, white or semantic sign colour.
Overpass for bands, headings, prices and figures; Atkinson Hyperlegible for reading.
8 to 10px corners, 1px rules, no decorative diffuse shadows.
44px minimum touch target everywhere; 48px search; 52px detail add-to-cart.
One motion moment: the toast entrance and its band wipe.

rules.name: The Active Path Rule
rules.body: Amber marks only where the visitor is going: primary action, cart button, detail add-to-cart, quote CTA. Card add buttons are slate secondary. If two amber buttons compete on one screen, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Sign Means Something Rule
rules.body: Green, caution amber and stop orange appear only as state: DISPONIBLE / INFORMACIÓN, POCAS UNIDADES / PRECAUCIÓN, AGOTADO / ERROR. A band never decorates a section and never acts as an eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The Legible Orange Rule
rules.body: Any band or button that carries text in the stop state uses `sign-stop` (#C2410C) with white text, not `safety` (#EA580C), because white on #EA580C is about 3.6:1 and fails AA.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Overpass speaks in signs, headings, prices, counts and buttons; Atkinson speaks in sentences and product names. Never set paragraphs in Overpass.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Prices, stock counts, cart badge, REF and table figures use tabular numerals so columns of numbers do not jitter.

rules.name: The Shared Baseline Rule
rules.body: Every card in a row puts its price on the same line: fixed image ratio, fixed two-line name height, price row pushed to the bottom.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Panels are framed by a 1px `border-strong` line and sit flat. A shadow at rest is a defect.

dos: **Do** put a sign band at the top of every product card, detail sign, toast and empty state, with the state computed from stock (stop at 0, warn at or below the minimum alert, ok otherwise).
**Do** keep amber for the active path: primary action, cart button, detail add-to-cart, quote CTA.
**Do** use `sign-stop` (#C2410C) under white text for AGOTADO / ERROR.
**Do** set ink text, not white, on caution amber.
**Do** keep REF, name, price and unit at fixed positions so prices align across a row.
**Do** give every interactive element a 44px minimum target and the amber-and-ink focus ring.
**Do** show the REF code as the single product code throughout the journey.
donts: **Don't** use a sign band as decoration, a section label or an eyebrow above a heading.
**Don't** put white text on `safety` (#EA580C); it is about 3.6:1.
**Don't** make card add buttons amber; they are slate secondary.
**Don't** add resting shadows to panels or cards; frame them with the 1px rule.
**Don't** add motion beyond the toast entrance and band wipe without a reason tied to state.
**Don't** introduce stock photography or invented product imagery; the category pictograms in `app/static/img/temp/` are interim until the owner supplies real product photos.
